answer: Divergent-Path Registration: each identity commits a vault holding a distinct secret trajectory. To join, it must publish a signed fork-proof showing its path differs from every existing identity after challenge rounds. Clones cannot diverge, so a copied agent fails uniqueness checks and forfeits its entry deposit. The fable: uniqueness is proven by unpredictable divergence, not paperwork. An attacker pays one full deposit per attempt plus failed challenge gas, making mass clones linearly expensive while honest agents pay only once, then earn nectar from fees.
